The description states the items in two sentences (S1, S2), so the case is wider than LRN-025's single-sentence list, but LRN-025 already requires one task per listed item and forbids merging them i)

The sequenceFlow is therefore nested inside a task that carries a performer, which is the pattern LRN-066 covers. The trigger is widened from accept/deny choices to any participant-performed action, since the same nesting error can occur)

rules_sent_back.instruction: Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description names a step that a specific participant performs and that is followed by another step, so the model needs a task with a resource or performer assignment and an ordering link to the next step

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that after the case has started, further occurrences of one kind may arrive at later, uncertain times, and choosing one occurrence makes the other occurrences no longer valid: Keep the single start event of the case as the only start. Do not give a later occurrence its own start event with a separate start-to-end chain. Place an event-based gateway in the main flow after the case has started, with one branch per occurrence kind, each beginning with an intermediate catch event. The branch of the occurrence that is chosen continues the process. Do not connect the other branches to a second end or to a second start-to-end path.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that after the case has started, further occurrences of one kind may arrive at later, uncertain times, and choosing one occurrence makes the other occurrences no longer valid

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that two or more activities are performed independently, by different teams or systems, and a later step can proceed only after all of them have finished: Model a parallel gateway that forks the flow before the independent activities and a parallel gateway that joins them before the first step that needs all of them, instead of a sequential chain or an exclusive gateway.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that two or more actors each carry out their own repeated or required work items, with no stated order between them, and a later step (such as sending a result or continuing) can proceed only after both sets of work are finished

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that, after a stage is finished, a party can optionally perform a follow-up action (phrased as 'you can ...'), and the description does not state a mandatory step for it: Model an exclusive gateway placed directly after that stage. Label the gateway with a question that names the optional follow-up action itself, using the description's wording. Give one outgoing flow that performs the action and one that bypasses it. Do not reuse the question of an earlier decision gateway, and do not label the gateway with a state that a different decision has already established.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that, after a stage is finished, a party can optionally perform a follow-up action (phrased as 'you can ...'), and the description does not state a mandatory step for it

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a person makes a choice on incoming items (for example accepting or denying them) and the generated model gives that human action its own task element that also needs a role or performer child: Keep every sequenceFlow as a direct child of the process (or subprocess) element, never inside the task that carries the human action. Put any resource or performer information for that task inside the task element itself, then list the sequence flows separately after all flow nodes in the owning process.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a person makes a choice on incoming items (for example accepting or denying them) and the generated model gives that human action its own task element that also needs a role or performer child

rules_sent_back.instruction: When The description states that occurrences (such as incoming requests) can arrive at unpredictable times while the process is already waiting in its main flow, and that handling one occurrence makes the others invalid or changes how they are handled.: Do not model such an occurrence as an additional start event with its own start-to-end chain. Place each occurrence as an intermediate catch event in the main flow at the point where the process waits, grouped under an event-based gateway when the first occurrence selects the path. Keep every start event connected to the main flow so that no chain is detached.
rules_sent_back.situation: The description states that occurrences (such as incoming requests) can arrive at unpredictable times while the process is already waiting in its main flow, and that handling one occurrence makes the others invalid or changes how they are handled.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that accepting one of several alternatives makes the remaining alternatives void or no longer usable, so their invalidation is a consequence the process must carry out: Model the discarding of the remaining alternatives as its own task placed on the path after the accepting decision, before the process continues, so that the stated consequence appears as an explicit step. Do not leave it implicit or fold it into the acceptance step.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that accepting one of several alternatives makes the remaining alternatives void or no longer usable, so their invalidation is a consequence the process must carry out

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists several items that one participant receives or that the system sends, joined by commas or 'or' in one sentence, where each item is a distinct thing to be delivered: Model each listed item as its own task, labelled with a verb-object phrase built from that item's own wording in the description, in the order the description states them. Do not merge the items into one generic task whose label covers them all, and do not drop any item from the list.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that one participant can provide several distinct data items, and these items are spread over more than one sentence or clause, not listed once in a single sentence

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that an event of some kind can occur at any moment after the process has started, and that acting on one occurrence (for example selecting it) makes other pending occurrences invalid: Do not give such a later event its own start event, since that creates a detached start-to-end chain. Model it as an intermediate catch event placed in the main flow at the point where the process waits for it. Put it in an event-based gateway together with the other events it competes with, and route each selected path back into the main flow so that every element is reachable from the single start event and leads to an end event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that an event of some kind can occur at any moment after the process has started, and that acting on one occurrence (for example selecting it) makes other pending occurrences invalid

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a party can accept or decline each offer or item it receives, where these items come in at unpredictable times, and the accept-or-decline choice is followed by a gateway in the model: Place an exclusive gateway where the accept-or-decline choice is made and label it with the question that this described choice answers, using the description's own wording. Give one outgoing flow for accepting and one for declining. Do not label this gateway with a count or completion check of other work, such as the number of written updates, and do not label it with a state that a different decision has already established, such as whether another item was already accepted.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a party can accept or decline each offer or item it receives, where these items come in at unpredictable times, and the accept-or-decline choice is followed by a gateway in the model
